NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
BYLAWS OF 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. 
A New York Charitable Not-for-Profit Corporation 
Adoption Date: __________________________________ 
ARTICLE I — NAME, OFFICE, AND PURPOSE 
Section 1.1. Name. The name of the corporation is North Horizon Foundation Inc. (the 
“Corporation”). 
Section 1.2. Principal Office. The principal office shall be located in Queens County, New 
York, at a place determined by the Board of Directors (the “Board”). The Corporation may 
maintain other offices as the Board determines. 
Section 1.3. Purpose. The Corporation is organized exclusively for charitable, educational, and 
cultural purposes within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. Its 
mission is to promote community welfare, cultural connection, social development, and 
educational enrichment, particularly for Nepalese and Nepalese-American individuals and 
communities, through needs-based assistance, outreach, referrals, training, media, arts, and 
community programs. 
Section 1.4. Limitations. No part of the Corporation’s net earnings shall inure to the benefit of 
any member, director, officer, or other private person, except that the Corporation may pay 
reasonable compensation for services actually rendered and make payments that further its 
exempt purposes. The Corporation shall not participate or intervene in any political campaign for 
or against a candidate for public office, and no substantial part of its activities shall consist of 
lobbying. All fundraising and revenue-producing activities shall be lawful, consistent with the 
Corporation’s exempt purposes, and used solely to advance those purposes. 
ARTICLE II — MEMBERSHIP, CONTRIBUTION TIERS, AND VOTING 
Section 2.1. Voting Members and Classes. The Corporation shall have voting members. 
Membership categories and voting power shall be based on the contribution tiers below, subject 
to applicable law, the Certificate of Incorporation, and these Bylaws. “Founding Members” are 
those identified in the Corporation’s organizational records. Founding Member status recognizes 
service in establishing the Corporation and, for voting purposes, carries the same voting power as 
Page 1 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
the Royal tier. Founding status does not create ownership rights or any right to distributions of 
Corporation assets. 
Section 2.2. Contribution Tiers and Votes. Unless changed by an amendment to these Bylaws, 
the contribution tiers and votes assigned to each eligible voting member are: 
Silver: contributions of $1,000–$2,499 — 1 vote. 
Gold: contributions of $2,500–$4,999 — 3 votes. 
Diamond: contributions of $5,000–$9,999 — 5 votes. 
Elite: contributions of $10,000–$24,999 — 15 votes. 
Royal: contributions of $25,000 or more — 25 votes. 
Founding Members: 25 votes, equivalent to the Royal tier. 
Section 2.3. Contribution Period and Administration. The Board shall adopt a written, 
consistently applied policy specifying the period in which contributions are measured, how 
contributions are credited, the process for confirming tier eligibility, membership admission and 
renewal, and any dues or administrative requirements. Until that policy is adopted, the Board 
shall not assign or change a member’s tier without a recorded Board decision applied 
consistently and in good faith. Contributions are not purchases of ownership, and no member 
may receive distributions of the Corporation’s income or assets by reason of a contribution. 
Section 2.4. Good Standing. A member is in good standing if the member satisfies the 
applicable eligibility and administrative requirements adopted by the Board, supports the 
Corporation’s mission, and complies with these Bylaws and Board policies. 
Section 2.5. Member Meetings and Elections. An annual meeting shall be held on a date fixed 
by the Board to elect directors and conduct other business. Special meetings may be called by the 
President, the Board, or members entitled to cast at least ten percent of all votes entitled to be 
cast. Notice shall state the date, time, place or electronic participation method, and, for a special 
meeting, its purpose. Notice shall be delivered as required by New York law. 
Section 2.6. Member Quorum and Voting. Members entitled to cast a majority of all votes 
entitled to be cast shall constitute a quorum. Unless a greater vote is required by law, the 
Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws, action by the members is approved by a majority 
of the votes cast at a meeting where a quorum is present. Each member’s votes shall be 
determined by the member’s tier under Section 2.2. Members may participate electronically 
Page 2 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
when authorized by the Board and conducted with reasonable identity verification, participation, 
and voting safeguards. 
Section 2.7. Suspension or Removal of Members. After reasonable notice and an opportunity 
to be heard, the Board may suspend or remove a member for material misconduct, failure to 
remain in good standing, or conduct substantially harmful to the Corporation, by a two-thirds 
vote of directors present at a meeting where a quorum is present. A director with a disqualifying 
conflict shall not participate in the decision. 
ARTICLE III — BOARD OF DIRECTORS 
Section 3.1. Authority. The Board shall manage the affairs, property, programs, and finances of 
the Corporation and shall exercise all corporate powers not reserved to the members by law, the 
Certificate of Incorporation, or these Bylaws. 
Section 3.2. Number and Qualifications. The Board shall consist of not fewer than seven (7) 
and not more than nine (9) directors. The number within that range may be changed by a vote of 
the members, subject to applicable law and the Certificate of Incorporation. Directors must be at 
least eighteen years old, committed to the Corporation’s mission, and eligible for at least the 
Diamond contribution tier under Article II. The Board shall apply the contribution-tier eligibility 
requirement consistently and in accordance with a written policy. A decrease in Board size shall 
not shorten an incumbent director’s term. 
Section 3.3. Election and Terms. Directors shall be elected by the voting members at the annual 
meeting. Each director shall serve a three-year term and until a successor is elected and qualified. 
Directors may be reelected. The Board may establish staggered terms by resolution, provided 
that any transition arrangement is lawful and does not unlawfully shorten an incumbent’s term. 
Section 3.4. Vacancies. A vacancy may be filled by a two-thirds vote of the remaining directors, 
to the extent permitted by New York law, even if fewer than a quorum remain. A director elected 
to fill a vacancy serves for the balance of the unexpired term and until a successor is elected and 
qualified. 
Section 3.5. Removal and Resignation. The voting members may remove a director, with or 
without cause, to the extent permitted by New York law. A director may resign by written or 
electronic notice to the President or Secretary; the resignation is effective when received unless a 
later date is stated. 
Section 3.6. Compensation. Directors shall not be compensated merely for serving as directors, 
but may receive reimbursement for reasonable expenses. A director may receive reasonable 
compensation for separate professional or employment services only when approved in advance 
by disinterested directors under Article VI. 
Page 3 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
ARTICLE IV — BOARD MEETINGS AND BOARD VOTING 
Section 4.1. Regular and Special Meetings. The Board shall meet at least six times each year 
unless the Board changes the meeting schedule by a two-thirds vote, provided the revised 
schedule remains consistent with applicable law and the Corporation’s needs. Special meetings 
may be called by the President or any two directors. 
Section 4.2. Notice. At least two days’ notice of a special Board meeting shall be given 
personally, by telephone, mail, or electronic transmission. Notice may be waived in writing or 
electronically, and attendance without timely objection constitutes waiver. The purpose need not 
be stated unless required by these Bylaws or law. 
Section 4.3. Quorum. A majority of the entire Board shall constitute a quorum. If a quorum is 
not present, no Board action may be taken except to adjourn the meeting. 
Section 4.4. Two-Thirds Board Approval Rule. Except where applicable law or the Certificate 
of Incorporation requires a different or greater vote, every action or resolution submitted for a 
vote of the Board must receive the affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the directors present 
and entitled to vote at a meeting where a quorum is present. If a vote is taken by unanimous 
written or electronic consent, all directors entitled to vote must consent as required by law. Any 
statutory requirement for approval by a specified proportion of the entire Board or by 
disinterested directors remains controlling. 
Section 4.5. Remote Participation and Written Consent. Directors may participate through 
conference telephone, video, or similar communications allowing all participants to hear one 
another at the same time and participate fully. Any action taken without a meeting must be by 
unanimous written or electronic consent, filed with the minutes, as required by New York law. 
ARTICLE V — OFFICERS 
Section 5.1. Officers and Election. The officers shall include a President, Vice President, 
Secretary, and Treasurer, and may include additional officers determined by the Board. Officers 
shall be elected annually by the Board and serve until their successors are elected and qualified. 
One person may hold more than one office, except that the President may not also serve as 
Secretary. 
Section 5.2. President. The President shall provide general leadership, preside at member and 
Board meetings unless a separate Chair is elected, oversee implementation of Board decisions, 
and perform other duties assigned by the Board. 
Page 4 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
Section 5.3. Secretary. The Secretary shall ensure that notices are given, minutes and 
membership records are maintained, corporate records are preserved, and required reports and 
documents are properly filed or presented to the Board. 
Section 5.4. Treasurer. The Treasurer shall oversee the Corporation’s funds, financial records, 
budgets, reports, banking arrangements, and required tax and regulatory filings, subject to Board 
supervision and any financial controls adopted by the Board. 
Section 5.5. Removal, Vacancies, and Compensation. The Board may remove an officer 
elected by the Board with or without cause and may fill any officer vacancy. Officers may 
receive reasonable compensation for services actually rendered when approved by disinterested 
directors and properly documented. 
ARTICLE VI — CONFLICTS OF INTEREST 
Section 6.1. Policy. The Board shall adopt and oversee a written conflict-of-interest policy 
consistent with New York law. Before initial election and annually thereafter, each director shall 
submit the disclosure statement required by that policy. 
Section 6.2. Disclosure And Recusal. Any director, officer, or key person with an actual or 
possible conflict or interest in a related-party transaction shall promptly disclose all material 
facts. That person shall not be present for or participate in deliberation or voting, shall not 
improperly influence the decision, and may provide background information only if requested 
before deliberations begin. 
Section 6.3. Approval And Records. A related-party transaction may be approved only if 
disinterested directors determine it is fair, reasonable, and in the Corporation’s best interest. 
Where required, available alternatives shall be considered. The minutes shall document the 
conflict, recusal, vote, alternatives considered, and basis for approval. 
ARTICLE VII — TEMPORARY COMMITTEES AND TASK GROUPS 
Section 7.1. Establishment And Purpose. A temporary committee or task group may be 
established when needed to complete a specific task or project that supports the Corporation’s 
mission. The committee’s assignment, scope, reporting expectations, and proposed duration shall 
be documented. 
Section 7.2. Supervisor And Formation. Each temporary committee or task group shall be 
supervised by a designated member approved by the Board. The supervising member may 
organize a group of volunteers or other participants as reasonably needed for the task, subject to 
Board policies, budget limits, conflict-of-interest requirements, and applicable law. 
Page 5 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
Section 7.3. Duration, Oversight, And Termination. The Board shall determine the duration of 
each temporary committee or task group and may extend, modify, suspend, or terminate it at any 
time by a two-thirds Board vote if the task is completed, no longer needed, outside the approved 
scope, inconsistent with the Corporation’s mission or requirements, or otherwise not in the 
Corporation’s best interests. A committee or task group may not bind the Corporation, incur 
expenses, sign contracts, or speak on behalf of the Corporation unless specifically authorized. 
Section 7.4. No Independent Board Authority. Temporary committees and task groups are 
advisory or operational bodies only and shall not exercise powers reserved by law to the Board, 
officers, or members. Any committee that is intended to exercise Board authority must be 
established and operated in compliance with New York law and these Bylaws. 
ARTICLE VIII — FINANCES AND RECORDS 
Section 8.1. Fiscal Year and Budget. The fiscal year shall end on December 31 unless changed 
by the Board. The Board shall approve an annual budget and exercise reasonable oversight of 
receipts, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and financial controls. 
Section 8.2. Banking And Contracts. Corporation funds shall be deposited in accounts 
approved by the Board. The Board shall authorize the individuals permitted to sign checks, 
approve electronic payments, enter contracts, or otherwise bind the Corporation, and may require 
two approvals for transactions above a threshold set by policy. 
Section 8.3. Books And Records. The Corporation shall maintain complete and accurate 
minutes, membership and Board records, financial records, its Certificate of Incorporation, these 
Bylaws, policies, and required filings. Records shall be retained and made available as required 
by law. 
ARTICLE IX — INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE 
Section 9.1. Indemnification. To the fullest extent permitted by New York law, the Corporation 
shall indemnify its directors and officers who act in good faith and in a manner reasonably 
believed to be in, or not opposed to, the Corporation’s best interests. The Corporation may 
purchase insurance to protect the Corporation and its directors, officers, employees, and agents. 
ARTICLE X — AMENDMENTS 
Section 10.1. Amendment. These Bylaws may be adopted, amended, or repealed by the voting 
members, subject to applicable law and the Certificate of Incorporation. The Board may also 
amend these Bylaws to the extent permitted by New York law and the Certificate of 
Incorporation; however, the members may amend or repeal any bylaw adopted by the Board. 
Notice of a proposed amendment shall include its text or a clear summary. 
Page 6 
ARTICLE XI — DISSOLUTION 
NORTH HORIZON FOUNDATION INC. | BYLAWS DRAFT 
Section 11.1. Distribution Of Assets. Upon dissolution, and after payment or provision for all 
liabilities, the Corporation’s remaining assets shall be distributed exclusively for one or more 
exempt purposes within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, or to the 
federal government or a state or local government for a public purpose, subject to the Certificate 
of Incorporation and all required governmental or court approvals. No remaining assets shall be 
distributed to any member, director, officer, or other private person. 
CERTIFICATE OF ADOPTION
